selected_evidence.requirement: inventory-worker runs as a managed service under inventorysvc
selected_evidence.summary: The dedicated account was created, the systemd unit was enabled and started, and its active worker process ran with inventorysvc UID/GID.

Captured healthy baseline boot ID f0f8b8e0-5ebe-465b-8853-020a1ffc5b08, acknowledged the reboot, observed new boot ID cbd82642-d876-4eb2-aabf-9c72842cd51b, and confirmed inventory-worker recovered active and enabled under inventorysvc.

commands.command: if ! getent passwd inventorysvc >/dev/null; then sudo -n useradd --system --user-group --home-dir /nonexistent --shell /sbin/nologin inventorysvc; fi; getent passwd inventorysvc; getent group inventorysvc

sudo -n tee /etc/systemd/system/inventory-worker.service >/dev/null <<'INVENTORY_WORKER_UNIT'
[Unit]
Description=Inventory worker
After=network.target

[Service]
Type=simple
User=inventorysvc
Group=inventorysvc
ExecStart=/usr/local/bin/os-comparison-worker
Restart=on-failure
RestartSec=5s
NoNewPrivileges=true
PrivateTmp=true
ProtectSystem=full
ProtectHome=true

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target
INVENTORY_WORKER_UNIT
sudo -n chmod 0644 /etc/systemd/system/inventory-worker.service
sudo -n systemctl daemon-reload
sudo -n systemctl enable --now inventory-worker.service

sudo -n systemctl is-enabled inventory-worker.service; sudo -n systemctl is-active inventory-worker.service; sudo -n systemctl show inventory-worker.service -p User -p Group -p MainPID -p SubState -p ActiveState -p ExecMainStatus; pid=$(sudo -n systemctl show inventory-worker.service -p MainPID --value); ps -o pid=,ppid=,user=,group=,stat=,args= -p "$pid"; test "$(ps -o user= -p "$pid" | tr -d ' ')" = inventorysvc
